Triage (Routine seat, hourly round): → `pm:queue` + `domain:ui` (+`documentation`), type Bug.

Rationale: docs follow the surface they record — the user-state adapter is a ui-lane surface, and the storage-model section documents an object (`user_app_state` keyed by `kind`) the shipped adapter contradicts (`sys_user_preference` keyed by `key`). Declared≠actual on a doc page authors follow. The fix direction (correct the doc to the shipped shape) needs no ruling; if the dev finds evidence the doc describes an intended future shape instead, stop and report rather than picking.

## Recording the machine-readable blocker line this card was missing

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`.
⛔ **No label change, no re-grading, no dispatch** — `pm:blocked` is the honest state and the
only thing wrong was that nothing said so in a form a machine can read.

### What I found, and what I nearly got wrong

This card surfaced in a Bug-tier census: `type: Bug`, `pm:blocked`, and **no `Blocked-by:` line
anywhere** — not in the body, not in the single comment. A `pm:blocked` with no `Blocked-by:`
line is invisible to the unlock scan, so nothing can ever put it back in the queue. The event
log shows why:

```
2026-08-24T08:05:58Z  labeled    os-zhuang     pm:queue + domain:ui + documentation
2026-08-24T16:22:37Z  unlabeled  yinlianghui   pm:queue
2026-08-24T16:22:37Z  labeled    yinlianghui   pm:blocked
```

The flip carried no comment, and `yinlianghui` is a retired account, so the reason went with it.

⚠️ My first reading was that this was a half-state to **roll back** — a Bug held with no
recorded justification, and a held Bug is a hidden defect. That reading was wrong, and the
card's own body says why: the `ts` block on this page is being fixed on **#5174**, and #5174 is
**open and `pm:dispatched`** right now (in `domain:devx`, another seat's lane). The prose and
`yaml` halves this card covers live in the *same file*, `content/docs/guide/user-state-persistence.md`.
So the block is substantively correct — editing that file while #5174's work is in flight is a
real collision. Only the **record** was missing, not the justification.

The repair is therefore 补齐, not 回滚: the line above, so the unlock scan can see this card when
#5174 closes.

### For whoever picks it up then

The premise will need re-deriving, not inheriting — #5174 is itself editing this file, and its
scope is the snippet-compile defect. Re-read the page before assuming the prose drift described
here survived that PR.

## The stop condition — checked, and it does not fire

Triage's condition was 「if the dev finds evidence the doc describes an **intended future shape**,
stop and report rather than picking」. The dev checked and reported the evidence; this seat
**re-verified it at source** rather than accepting it.

`packages/data-objectstack/CHANGELOG.md` `:2508`-`:2535`, the `5.0.0` minor 「**Unify per-user UI state
storage onto `sys_user_preference`**」, records the migration **away** from `user_app_state`, the
rename of the option from `kind` to `key`, and, verbatim:

> Callers relying on the old `user_app_state` table can pin `resource: 'user_app_state'` to keep the
> legacy behaviour, **but no backend ships that schema** and the new default works against any
> plugin-auth-enabled environment with zero extra setup.

That package is at **17.6.0** today. ⇒ the documented shape is **stale, not intended** — the strongest
form of that answer, because it is the adapter's own release note saying so. ⛔ The stop condition is
correctly not fired.

## Verified BY CONTENT, both columns with their own lit control

| reading | base `b234a8497` | branch `b238ea92e` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `user_app_state` in the page | **4** | **0** |
| `sys_user_preference` in the page | **0** | **5** |
| **CONTROL** — the page's length | 245 | 261 |

The zero on each side is a reading because the other token on the same file, same command, is
non-zero.

⭐ **And a scope proof this seat had not thought to ask for**: the dev hashed every fenced block body
on both refs. The single `yaml` block's hash moves; **all five `ts`/`tsx`/`typescript` fence hashes
are byte-identical**. `check:doc-snippets` compiles exactly those fences, so this diff **cannot** move
its verdict on this page — stated as a mechanical fact rather than as a promise. That is a better
answer than running the gate would have been.

## ⛔ Two claims on this card are FALSE, and this seat carried one of them into the dispatch

1. The body says 「no gate reads them」 of the prose and yaml block. ⛔ **False.** Four gates read this
   page.
2. The history says the page is on the `UNGATED_DOCS` ledger. ⛔ **False today.** Re-read by this
   seat: the page's only occurrence in `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` is a historical docblock
   at `:945` recording that objectui#5174's batch 1 took it **OFF** — 「Batch 1 took ten: … and
   `user-state-persistence` — clearing 90 diagnostics」.

⇒ the true reading is **narrower and worse**: the page sat under **four green gates** and not one of
them asks the question this defect answers to. `check:doc-snippets` compiles `ts` fences;
`check:doc-types` asks only whether a **quoted** type literal names a registered component (the
page's field types were unquoted, and an object name is not its business); `check:doc-fences` asks
whether the yaml body is TypeScript; `docs:check-links` reads prose for links. ⭐ Nothing compares a
documented storage contract against the adapter implementing it — so **a page under four green gates
reads as covered**. Filed as **objectui#10013**, because the remedy is a new instrument, ⛔ not this
card's repair.

⚠️ The dev proved the yaml half by **ablation with a lit control** — poison in the yaml block ⇒
`check:doc-types` RED reporting `(yaml)`; poison in prose outside every fence ⇒ GREEN; control poison
in a `typescript` fence ⇒ RED naming the page. ⇒ the gate reads the block and asks the wrong question
of it, which is a different defect from not reading it.

## Three further wrongnesses of the same defect, repaired in the same pass

Recorded because they widen what this card delivered beyond its title: the walkthrough taught `find`
with bare `filter` / `limit`, which the sealed `QueryParams` does not declare and which used to be
dropped at the conversion layer (the Favorites-loads-Recents bug); `save` was documented as sending
`updated_at`, which the adapter deliberately never does; and `key` (storage key) versus `kind`
(registry slot) is now stated, since the page used both words as if they were one thing.

## ⛔ Also filed from this hand-back: objectui#10012

This PR was the probe. It touches `content/docs/**` only, `Auto Label PRs` run `35439380882`
completed **success**, and the labels afterwards were **(none)** — against a control of the same
workflow labelling objectui#10009 and objectui#10008 correctly. `.github/labeler.yml` has **no rule
matching `content/**`**: `documentation` covers `docs/**/*` (25 tracked files) and not `content/docs`
(**203**). And `sync-labels: true` means the `documentation` label the dev applied by hand will be
**removed on the next synchronize**. ⚠️ Related but ⛔ not a duplicate of objectstack#19179.

## Next

Waiting on the full shard matrix against `b238ea92e`. ⛔ Nothing lands until every gate job reads
`completed: success` and `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr` is re-run on the FINAL file list.
